headlines.text: 2021 brought us this moment: the AEW World Tag Team Titles found a new home as The Lucha Brothers vs. The Young Bucks battled it out in a Steel Cage match, appearing on All Out, rated 9.49 ? the kind of match that redefines a wrestler's career ? ending the champion's reign at 10 defenses. A five-star classic inside a steel cage ? the Lucha Brothers entered to their theme song performed live for the first time, and delivered a war good enough to earn a perfect rating, dethroning the champions to capture their first AEW World Tag Team Titles.

It was 2020 when there was a changing of the guard for the AEW World Tag Team Titles as FTR vs. Omega & Page battled it out, appearing on All Out, rated 7.73 ? a good, competitive contest ? ending the champion's reign at 7 defenses. It was the first title opportunity of FTR's career. A changing of the guard in the tag division ? FTR, fresh off leaving WWE earlier that year, dethroned the reigning champions in a near-30-minute battle to capture their first AEW gold.
2025 brought us this moment: Konosuke Takeshita vs. Mark Briscoe closed out Collision, rated 8.02 ? an excellent showing.

secondaries.text: On a Saturday in 2026, back when Alex Shelley made their long-awaited comeback after 4 years away, appearing on Collision.

It was 2021 when Kenny Omega vs. Christian Cage put the AEW World Heavyweight Title on the line, appearing on All Out, rated 8.16 ? a genuinely great match. A hard-fought main event capping a stacked night that also saw three separate AEW debuts (Ruby Soho, Adam Cole, and Bryan Danielson) ? Omega successfully defended his title in a match many called one of the best of the entire show.

Flash back to 2021, when Miro vs. Eddie Kingston clashed for the AEW TNT Title, appearing on All Out, rated 7.55 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle. This stood as the 30th match in AEW TNT Title history ? a real landmark for that championship. The opening match of a show many later called an all-timer ? Miro successfully defended the TNT Title in a hard-hitting contest that set the tone for one of AEW's most stacked pay-per-view cards ever.
